title: A rollout plan
scenario: You are the COO of a regional bank with 3,500 staff in 60 branches. An AI assistant that drafts loan letters for branch staff passed its pilot with a clear go. The board wants it rolled out to every branch over the next year, and you must write the rollout plan. The exhibit holds the draft and what you know. All numbers are made up for this case.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  The letter assistant uses Anthropic's API.
  The document-search tool uses OpenAI's API.
  Wave 1 (200 staff in 4 branches) went live three weeks ago.

POLICY NOTE:
  Rule today: "Customer data goes only to tools covered by our zero data
  retention (ZDR) arrangement." The bank has ZDR with Anthropic for its
  main organization.
  Wave 2 plan: move the letter assistant to Claude Fable 5.1.
  Anthropic's data retention page (checked 2026-10-06) lists that model among
  those that "require 30-day data retention and are not available under ZDR
  unless expressly authorized by Anthropic".

DATA NOTE:
  Legal now requires customer documents in the search tool to be stored in
  the EU. The tool uses an OpenAI API project created last year with
  Global geography (no region set). The bank has not yet asked OpenAI about data residency.

WAVES (draft):
  Wave 1   200 staff    live
  Wave 2   400 staff    Starts: after wave 1    Stop rule: none    Owner: IT team
  Wave 3   3,500 staff  next quarter

INCIDENT (wave 1, Tuesday):
  Two letters sent to customers held another customer's loan balance.
  Known: 2 letters. Not known: the cause, or whether more letters are affected.
  The logs have not been checked yet.
  The team wants to write to the affected customers today.

ROADMAP LINE:
  Loan-letter assistant | medium tier | Now: wave 1 | named owner
  Stop rule, set before wave 1: pause if more than 2% of letters have a wrong figure.
  Week 3 check of 200 sent letters: 18 had a wrong figure (9%).

questions.prompt: What should the policy owner do about the plan to use this model in wave 2?

options.text: Allow it, because the signed ZDR arrangement means customer data is safe in every model the bank uses today.
options.explanation: Anthropic's page lists this model as not available under ZDR unless Anthropic expressly authorizes it. ZDR does not cover every model.

options.text: Ban the model for every use, because a bank policy can never allow a model that keeps data for 30 days.
options.explanation: A ban goes further than the page does. The bank's legal team can decide whether 30-day retention is acceptable for a use.

options.text: Keep customer data out of that model unless legal approves 30-day retention, and name models in the rule.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's page says this model requires 30-day retention. "We have ZDR" is not a complete rule, so the policy should name what it covers.

options.text: Allow it, and tell staff to delete their chats after 30 days so that the vendor's copy is removed too.
options.explanation: Nothing on the page says that staff deleting chats removes the vendor's 30-day copy. The retention comes from the model's own terms.

questions.prompt: The search tool's OpenAI project has no region set. What fits OpenAI's data controls page for the EU rule?

options.text: Create a new project with the EU region selected, after OpenAI confirms that the bank is eligible.
options.explanation: Right. The page says regional storage is set by choosing a region when you create a new project, and to contact OpenAI's sales team for eligibility. Regions outside the US also need extra approvals.

options.text: Switch residency on in the old project's settings, so that its earlier files move to the EU as well.
options.explanation: The page describes choosing a region when you create a new project. It does not describe moving an existing project's data.

options.text: Do nothing more: once residency is on, OpenAI keeps every kind of the bank's data in the chosen region.
options.explanation: The page says residency does not apply to system data, such as account information, usage statistics and billing information.

options.text: Add the EU domain prefix to each request from the old project, which then stores its data in the EU.
options.explanation: The page says the prefix with a Global project's key selects regional processing for that request. Regional storage is set by choosing a region when you create a new project, so the old project's documents are not stored in the EU.

questions.prompt: What may the first message to the affected customers say?

options.text: No other customer's data was affected, and our technical team has already fixed the problem earlier this week.
options.explanation: Nobody knows yet whether more letters are affected, and the logs are unchecked. A letter should hold only facts that have been checked.

options.text: A staff member made a mistake while using the assistant, and the bank is now dealing with that person directly.
options.explanation: The cause is not known. Blaming a person without facts is a guess, and the write-up should be about the system.

options.text: The problem came from our AI vendor's system, and the vendor has confirmed in writing that it will not happen again.
options.explanation: The cause is not known, and no vendor has confirmed anything. Do not guess in a customer letter.

options.text: We sent a letter on Tuesday with another customer's loan balance, and we are investigating and will update you Friday.
options.explanation: Right. It says only what is known, and promises an update. The course says not to guess in a customer letter.

questions.prompt: Which rewrite of the wave 2 line fits the course's wave model best?

options.text: Starts on the first Monday of next month, as planned. Stops if finance runs out of budget. Owner: the IT team as a whole, with no single lead.
options.explanation: A date is not a gate. A budget stop is not a safety stop, and a team is not one named person.

options.text: Starts when wave 1 meets its go rule and support is stable. Stops on a serious incident. Owner: one named person at the bank.
options.explanation: Right. A wave needs an entry gate, a stop rule and one named owner. This line has all three.

options.text: Starts when wave 1 users ask for more of their colleagues. Stops if 10% of staff complain. Owner: the steering group of department heads.
options.explanation: Demand from users is not an entry gate, and a group does not give one named owner.

options.text: Starts after wave 1 ends, whatever the results. Stops if the vendor has an outage. Owner: the vendor's account manager for the bank.
options.explanation: "Whatever the results" is not an entry gate, and the owner must be a person at the bank. A vendor outage is only one reason to stop.

questions.prompt: The week 3 check passed the stop rule's limit. What should the roadmap do?

options.text: Keep the item in Now with its dates, and fix the wrong figures while wave 1 keeps running as it is.
options.explanation: The stop rule was set to pause the wave at this point. Running on ignores the rule that was written for this case.

options.text: Wait for the quarterly review, because the roadmap should change only on its planned review dates.
options.explanation: The course lists a pilot reaching its stop rule as a reason to review the roadmap early.

options.text: Review the roadmap now, and move the item to a Stopped list with the reason, until it is fixed.
options.explanation: Right. A Stopped list with reasons is a good result: it shows that the stop rule worked.

options.text: Remove the item and say nothing, so that the board sees a roadmap with only items that are going well.
options.explanation: Hiding it removes what the board needs to know. A roadmap should show what was stopped and why.
